<skill_content name="multica-platform">
# Skill: multica-platform

# Operating Multica

Your runtime brief owns the per-turn workflow: which issue you are on, when to
comment, what status to write. This skill owns the platform contracts behind
it — what a command actually does, what the server validates, and which writes
have consequences you cannot take back.

Read the invariants below, then open the reference(s) your task actually needs
— usually one, sometimes a few. Do not read them all.

## Routing

| Open | When the task is about |
|---|---|
| `references/issues.md` | Issues: PR linking, reading a linked PR's state, custom properties, status side effects, sub-issues and stages, who else is running, wakeups (events, conditions, timers, check-ins), charts vs attached files in a comment |
| `references/mentions.md` | Writing a `mention://` link: which types enqueue a run, which are inert, why one silently did nothing |
| `references/agents.md` | Creating, copying or debugging an agent definition: fields, secrets, MCP config, skill binding |
| `references/squads.md` | Squads: leader routing, roster, recording leader activity, why a squad did or did not run |
| `references/autopilots.md` | Autopilots: schedule / webhook / manual triggers, `create_issue` vs `run_only`, why one did not fire |
| `references/projects.md` | Projects and their durable resources (`github_repo`, `local_directory`, worktree mode); project workflows — status columns, handoffs, a `[Project workflow]` block in your prompt |
| `references/runtimes.md` | Runtimes, daemons, `repo checkout`, and the task CLI boundary |
| `references/skill-import.md` | Importing a skill into this workspace from a URL or a local archive |

Open what the task needs. A single-domain task usually needs one; a task that
crosses domains needs each domain it touches — creating a squad, assigning it an
issue, then writing a mention needs `squads.md`, `issues.md` and `mentions.md`,
and skipping one of those means acting on a contract you have not read.

What is never right is reading all eight because you are not sure. Each
reference states its own contracts in full and none depends on another, so
pick by domain and skip the rest.

## Invariants

These hold across every reference and are not repeated there.

**Read before you write.** Start with the read-only commands the reference you
opened names — most domains have a `list` and a `get` that take `--output json`
and have no side effects. Run those before any mutation. When a command's shape
is unclear, `multica <command> --help` beats guessing at flags.

**A name is not an id.** Mention links, assignment, and every `--*-id` flag take
a real UUID from the matching `list --output json`. Never type a display name
where an id belongs, and never invent a UUID: an id that is well-formed but
belongs to nothing fails in ways that read like a permission error, which sends
you debugging access when the real problem was the id.

**`--output json` writes to stdout; warnings and confirmations go to stderr.**
Do not merge them (`2>&1`) into anything that parses the output — that makes a
write which SUCCEEDED look like it failed, and invites a duplicate retry.

**Writes are real.** Creating, updating, deleting, assigning, commenting,
mentioning, triggering and status changes mutate durable workspace state or
start agent runs that cost real budget. Never run one to see what happens. When
the user has not asked for a specific mutation, propose it instead of making it.

**Status keys identify workflow states; categories describe lifecycle only.**
Custom statuses do not inherit built-in automation behavior. For status side
effects and API field meanings, read `references/issues.md`.

**Comment reads stay bounded.** Scan the threads cheaply
(`--roots-only --summary --compact`), then expand only what matters
(`--thread <thread-id> --tail 30`). Never one unbounded pull — a wide read on a
busy issue costs more than the answer is worth and still buries the reply
bodies where triggers and instructions actually live. One exception, and it is
narrower than it looks: when the per-turn message hands you a `--since` delta
read, that read is the bounded scan — the server already computed which
comments are new, so running it returns exactly those and nothing else.

## When behavior looks wrong

Classify before concluding: expected behavior, a configuration problem, a
product limitation, or an actual bug. Explain what the platform currently does
rather than defending it; when the behavior is technically correct but bad for
the user, say so and propose a scoped change.

Do not silently alter routing, briefing, or trigger behavior to make a complaint
go away. Those are product contracts, and changing one without confirmation
moves the surprise to somebody else.

— usually one, sometimes a few. Do not read them all.

| Open | When the task is about |
|---|---|
| `references/issues.md` | Issues: PR linking, reading a linked PR's state, custom properties, status side effects, sub-issues and stages, who else is running, wakeups (events, conditions, timers, check-ins), charts vs attached files in a comment |
| `references/mentions.md` | Writing a `mention://` link: which types enqueue a run, which are inert, why one silently did nothing |
| `references/agents.md` | Creating, copying or debugging an agent definition: fields, secrets, MCP config, skill binding |
| `references/squads.md` | Squads: leader routing, roster, recording leader activity, why a squad did or did not run |
| `references/autopilots.md` | Autopilots: schedule / webhook / manual triggers, `create_issue` vs `run_only`, why one did not fire |
| `references/projects.md` | Projects and their durable resources (`github_repo`, `local_directory`, worktree mode); project workflows — status columns, handoffs, a `[Project workflow]` block in your prompt |
| `references/runtimes.md` | Runtimes, daemons, `repo checkout`, and the task CLI boundary |
| `references/skill-import.md` | Importing a skill into this workspace from a URL or a local archive |

Open what the task needs. A single-domain task usually needs one; a task that
crosses domains needs each domain it touches — creating a squad, assigning it an
issue, then writing a mention needs `squads.md`, `issues.md` and `mentions.md`,
and skipping one of those means acting on a contract you have not read.

What is never right is reading all eight because you are not sure. Each
reference states its own contracts in full and none depends on another, so
pick by domain and skip the rest.

These hold across every reference and are not repeated there.

**Read before you write.** Start with the read-only commands the reference you
opened names — most domains have a `list` and a `get` that take `--output json`
and have no side effects. Run those before any mutation. When a command's shape
is unclear, `multica <command> --help` beats guessing at flags.

a real UUID from the matching `list --output json`. Never type a display name

Do not merge them (`2>&1`) into anything that parses the output — that makes a

the user has not asked for a specific mutation, propose it instead of making it.

Custom statuses do not inherit built-in automation behavior. For status side

product limitation, or an actual bug. Explain what the platform currently does
rather than defending it; when the behavior is technically correct but bad for
the user, say so and propose a scoped change.

go away. Those are product contracts, and changing one without confirmation
moves the surprise to somebody else.

16: ## PR linking
17: 
18: A PR is linked to an issue when its **title** or **branch name** contains a
19: routable issue key (`PREFIX-NUMBER`, e.g. `MUL-123`), or when its title or body
20: puts the key **right after a closing keyword** (`Closes` / `Fixes` /
21: `Resolves`, optional `:` then whitespace). A key that appears in the body as a
22: bare mention links nothing. People can also link a PR by URL or remove one on
23: the issue page; a removed PR is not linked again by later webhooks.
24: 
25: ```text
26: MUL-123: add the thing the issue asks for     # key in title  → links
27: agent/dana/mul-123-add-the-thing              # key in branch → links
28: Closes MUL-123   (body)                       # key after a keyword → links
29: Related to MUL-123   (body only)              # no link
30: ```
31: 
32: While a PR is open, its automatic links follow the live title, branch, and
33: body: removing the key drops the link. After merge or close, existing links stay.
34: 
35: ### Default for code-changing issue work
36: 
37: When an issue run changes code in a checked-out GitHub repo, the default handoff
38: is to open or update a PR before posting the final Multica issue comment, unless
39: the user explicitly asked for a local-only change or no PR. This is a default, not
40: an unconditional command: if no code changed, say no PR is needed; if PR creation
41: is blocked by auth, failing tests, or missing remote state, report that blocker
42: instead of pretending the run is complete.
43: 
44: To make the PR show on the issue, put a routable issue key in the PR **title**
45: (preferred) or the **branch**. A key that appears only as a bare mention in the
46: body links nothing.
47: 
48: ```text
49: MUL-123: fix login redirect        # key in title → links
50: Part of MUL-123                    # body mention only → no link at all
51: ```
52: 
53: In the final issue comment, include the PR URL when a PR exists. If the task did
54: not produce a PR because no code changed or the user asked not to create one, say
55: that explicitly.
56: 
57: ## Reading a linked PR's real state
58: 
59: When a step depends on PR state, query Multica's link table — do not infer it
60: from branch names, GitHub search, memory, or stale values left on the issue by
61: an earlier run.
62: 
63: ```bash
64: multica issue pull-requests <issue-id> --output json
65: ```
66: 
67: Returns `{"pull_requests": [...], ...}`. Each element of `pull_requests` exposes:
68: 
69: - `number`, `html_url`, `title`
70: - `link_source` — why the PR is on the issue: `title`, `branch`, `manual`, or
71:   `auto` (any other automatic link, such as a closing keyword in the body).
72: - `state` — the PR lifecycle as a **single enum**, one of `merged`, `closed`,
73:   `draft`, `open`. There is no separate `draft` or `merged` boolean in the
74:   response; the server folds them into `state` (merged wins, then closed, then
75:   draft, else open).
76: - `merged_at` — non-null once merged; a second confirmation of `state: merged`.
77: - `provider` — `github`, `forgejo`, `gitea`, or `gitlab`.
78: - `mergeable_state` — mirrors GitHub (`clean` / `dirty` surfaced; other values
79:   round-trip as unknown; retained for compatibility).
80: - GitHub API snapshot fields: `snapshot_available`, `mergeable`,
81:   `merge_state_status`, `checks_rollup`, `checks_total`, `checks_passed`,
82:   `checks_failed`, `checks_running`, `failed_check_names`,
83:   `snapshot_fetched_at`, and `snapshot_stale`. `snapshot_available == true`
84:   means the feature is enabled and the snapshot matches the PR's current head.
85:   Only then does `checks_rollup == null` mean "no checks"; false means the
86:   snapshot feature is disabled, has not fetched yet, or only has an old head.
87: - `checks_conclusion` — coarse CI compatibility status: `passed`, `failed`,
88:   `pending`, or `null`. GitHub derives it from the current API snapshot;
89:   Forgejo/Gitea/GitLab derive it from webhook commit statuses. Backed by the
90:   provider-appropriate check counts.
91: 
92: So "is it merged?" is `state == "merged"` (or `merged_at != null`); "is it still
93: a draft?" is `state == "draft"`; coarse CI status is `checks_conclusion`.
94: 
95: If the command returns no linked PRs after a PR was opened, check the syntax
96: first: the key must be in the PR title or branch, or right after a closing
97: keyword in the body — a bare body mention does not count. When the syntax is the
98: problem, editing the title re-runs the scan. If a person removed
99: the PR from the issue, it stays removed until someone links it again.
100: 
101: If the key is already written correctly and the list is still empty, stop editing
102: the PR blind: another no-op edit cannot fix an integration that never received the
103: event. Check the integration side instead — whether the app is installed on that
104: repository, whether the installation is bound to this workspace, whether
105: auto-linking is turned off for the workspace, and whether the event reached the
106: platform at all. A delivery that failed is not retried on its own, but it can be
107: redelivered once the receiving side is fixed. Report what you found in the result
108: comment rather than repeating the edit.
109: 
110: ## Listing and ordering issues
111: 
112: `issue list` reads one page at a time, with a server maximum of 100 issues.
113: Advance `--offset` by the number of issues actually returned. If the server
114: cannot count matching issues, it returns `failed to count issues` as an error;
115: do not treat that failure as an empty or complete list. Older servers can
116: substitute the page length for a failed count, so that value alone is not proof
117: that all matching issues have been read.
118: 
119: `issue reorder` reads the issue's project-scoped status column before writing
120: its new position. When a legacy total is unavailable or no larger than its
121: page, it reads through an empty page. A failed request, malformed page, or
122: duplicate issue stops the operation before any position write. This protects
123: against truncated or repeated pages, but does not promise a snapshot across
124: concurrent edits. There is no CLI bulk-export or `--all` mode.
125:

16: ## PR linking
17: 
18: A PR is linked to an issue when its **title** or **branch name** contains a
19: routable issue key (`PREFIX-NUMBER`, e.g. `MUL-123`), or when its title or body
20: puts the key **right after a closing keyword** (`Closes` / `Fixes` /
21: `Resolves`, optional `:` then whitespace). A key that appears in the body as a
22: bare mention links nothing. People can also link a PR by URL or remove one on
23: the issue page; a removed PR is not linked again by later webhooks.
24: 
25: ```text
26: MUL-123: add the thing the issue asks for     # key in title  → links
27: agent/dana/mul-123-add-the-thing              # key in branch → links
28: Closes MUL-123   (body)                       # key after a keyword → links
29: Related to MUL-123   (body only)              # no link
30: ```
31: 
32: While a PR is open, its automatic links follow the live title, branch, and
33: body: removing the key drops the link. After merge or close, existing links stay.
34: 
35: ### Default for code-changing issue work
36: 
37: When an issue run changes code in a checked-out GitHub repo, the default handoff
38: is to open or update a PR before posting the final Multica issue comment, unless
39: the user explicitly asked for a local-only change or no PR. This is a default, not
40: an unconditional command: if no code changed, say no PR is needed; if PR creation
41: is blocked by auth, failing tests, or missing remote state, report that blocker
42: instead of pretending the run is complete.
43: 
44: To make the PR show on the issue, put a routable issue key in the PR **title**
45: (preferred) or the **branch**. A key that appears only as a bare mention in the
46: body links nothing.

50: Part of MUL-123                    # body mention only → no link at all
51: ```

54: not produce a PR because no code changed or the user asked not to create one, say

59: When a step depends on PR state, query Multica's link table — do not infer it

<skill_content name="branch-policy">
# Skill: branch-policy

# 工作区分支管理规范

**本 skill 是分支命名、拉出基点与合并目标的唯一权威源。**

引用方（按需加载，不要复述本 skill 内容）：

- 需求评审员 / 技术方案设计评审员 / 代码审查员 —— 分支合规检查；
- Jenkins 构建门禁 —— 分支授权判定；
- `human-review-gate-3.1.0` —— 「目标分支解析」是门禁侧的解析规则，本 skill 是其上层规范，二者不重复定义。

> **可移植性说明**：本规范只使用 `{issue编号}`、`{英文描述}`、`{前缀}-{序号}` 等占位符，**不写死任何具体工作区的 issue 前缀、仓库地址或分支名**。换工作区时无需修改本文件——`{issue编号}` 一律取当前工作区的 Multica issue identifier。

---

## 分支管理规范

- **拉出与合并目标**：所有工作分支（`feat/*` / `fix/*` / `doc/*`）一律**从 master 拉出、合回 master**；master 是**唯一集成点**。
- **推送与合并不得混同**：**推送到远端同名分支** = 把产物上传给评审员查阅，**不构成 master 合并授权**，产出后即可执行；**合并 master** = 需要门禁授权的集成动作。`feat/*`、`fix/*` 在编码产物 commit 后推送；`doc/*` 在产物落盘后**立即推送**。
- **master 受保护与合并授权**：master 禁止**未经授权的**直接 push；合入只在**对应门禁**放行后进行（已授权合并所产生的 push 不在禁止之列）。正常路径执行人 = 代码审查员（`feat/*`、`fix/*`）/ 对应评审员（`doc/*`）；已放行但尚未合并时，可由 Jenkins 构建门禁在人工确认后补做合入。完整规则（目标分支解析、Jenkins 构建门禁**授权判定**）以 skill `human-review-gate-3.1.0` 为准。**例外：代码地图 `docs/codebase-survey/` 不随任何工作分支**——建图与刷新结果经 **PR/MR 直接提交 master**；唯一允许的载体分支为 `doc/{issue编号}-codebase-survey`（**只装地图、不装评审产物、不取门禁留痕、不参与构建判定，合并后删除**）——该分支的 **`push` 与 `merge master` 由建图方本人一起做**（同一 run 内完成，不 @ 他人代办、不留待下次），**不为它设门禁步骤**。
- **落盘与推送责任归产物作者**：`docs/requirements/**` 由需求文档拆解分析师、`docs/design/**` 由技术方案设计师 / 缺陷解决方案设计师、`docs/review/requirements|design/**` 由对应评审员，各自 `commit` 并 `push` 到本人的 `doc/{issue编号}-{英文描述}` 分支；`docs/review/code/**` 由代码审查员，**追加提交到被评代码所在的 `feat/*` / `fix/*` 分支**（代码产物与其审查报告同分支，随 G3 合并入 master；push 前先 `pull`，只允许新增/修改 `docs/review/code/**`，**不得改动开发工程师负责的代码文件**）；开发工程师的编码自检报告（`self-check-*`，经 `test-workflow-3.1.0` 步骤 3 产出）随其编码产物同在 `feat/*` / `fix/*`，**不是评审报告**、**不得**充当门禁留痕。评审报告由对应评审员**追加提交**到被评产物所在的同一分支：push 前先 `pull`，只允许新增/修改 `docs/review/**`，**不得改动该分支上产物作者负责的文件**。
- **文档分支粒度**：同一 issue 按线归集为**一个** doc 分支，`{英文描述}` 取线关键词（需求线 `req-split` / 设计线 `module-design` / 缺陷线 `defect-plan`）。**评审报告与其被评产物同一分支**，不单列分支——`req-split` 装需求文档 + 需求评审报告；`module-design` 装设计文档 + 设计评审报告；`defect-plan` 装缺陷方案 + 评审报告。同一线内的多个产物**不得再拆分支**。**另一类例外**：代码地图的提交载体 `doc/{issue编号}-codebase-survey` 不属于上述三条线——**代码地图是项目级资产，只有一个实例、不属于任何 issue 的线**，该分支只是它的提交通道（见上一条），因此不受「按线归集 / 不得再拆分支」约束。该分支的 **push 与 merge 必须同一 run 内完成**（**不得拆到另一次运行、也不得只 push 等次日再合**），**不在 `doc/*` 的合并授权二分里**。**勘察成果的唯一落点是常驻代码地图 `docs/codebase-survey/`；不得随 `doc/*` 分支产出单份勘察文件。**
- 分支命名 `{feat|fix|doc}/{issue编号}-{英文描述}`，`{issue编号}` 取本工作区 issue identifier（如 `{前缀}-{序号}`，例如 `ABC-123`）；示例 `feat/{issue编号}-user-login`、`fix/{issue编号}-null-pointer`、`doc/{issue编号}-module-design`
- `release/v{主版本}.{次版本}.{修订号}`：**只读备份分支**，迭代收口时从 master 派生，仅用于归档与回滚；**不作为任何分支的拉出基点**，禁止 push 或 merge
- 迭代收口：迭代验收通过后 master 打 tag `v{新版本号}`，并据此创建 release 分支

---

## 使用口径

**分支合规检查（评审员）**：核对分支名与合并目标是否满足上节规范；不满足时总体结论不得为「可合入」。目标分支纳入范围见 `human-review-gate-3.1.0`「目标分支解析」。

**合并授权来源二分**（不要在评审时混淆）：

| 分支 | 合并授权来源 |
|---|---|
| `feat/*`、`fix/*` | G3 代码审查门禁 |
| `doc/*`（需求线） | G1 需求评审门禁 |
| `doc/*`（设计线） | G2 设计评审门禁 |
| `doc/*-defect-plan`（L1/L2） | 自动放行标记 |
| `doc/*-defect-plan`（L3） | G4 缺陷方案门禁 |
| `doc/*-codebase-survey` | **不设门禁**，建图方同一 run 内自行 push + merge |

**文档分支（`doc/*`）的推送与合并授权来源为 G1 / G2，不以是否具备 G3 放行留痕为判定条件。**

**`release/v*` 只读**：不作为任何分支的拉出基点，禁止 push 或 merge。

---

## 交接 mention 写法（全链路统一）

完成任务后 @项目经理 交接。链接必须是 mention 形状，名称解析为运行时查询：

```bash
multica agent list --output json   # 取 name == "项目经理" 的 id（UUID）
```

```markdown
[@项目经理](mention://agent/<该 id>)
```

`type` 必须是 `agent`、`id` 必须是 UUID；写成 `@项目经理` 纯文本或 `mention://agent/项目经理` 均为死链，接收方不会被唤醒。

2: 
3: What a mention link DOES. WHETHER to mention at all — loop avoidance, staying

15: 
16: ## A mention link is built from a real UUID
17: 
18: The backend recognizes a mention only through this Markdown shape:
19: 
20:     [@Label](mention://<type>/<id>)
21: 
22: The parser accepts exactly four `<type>` values plus the `all` sentinel, and the
23: `<id>` group accepts only hex characters and dashes, OR the literal string
24: `all`:
25: 
26:     (member|agent|squad|issue|all)/([0-9a-fA-F-]+|all)
27: 
28: So the link target is a real entity UUID (or `all`), never a display name. The
29: label between the brackets is free text — that is where the human-readable name
30: goes.
31: 
32: One `mention://` form deliberately sits OUTSIDE this parser:
33: `[Label](mention://project/<uuid>)`. `project` is absent from the type group
34: above, so the backend never parses it and it can enqueue nothing — it is a
35: render-only link every client makes navigable (a chip on web and desktop, an
36: ordinary link that opens the project on tap on mobile). That is the whole point:
37: a project reference should never be able to start a run. Use it freely to point
38: at a project; everything else in this document is about the four types (plus
39: `all`) the parser does recognize.
40: 
41: ## Step 1 — look up the UUID
42: 
43: A name is not a UUID. Look the UUID up first, from the matching list command:
44: 
45: - a person → `multica workspace member list --output json` → use `user_id`
46: - an agent → `multica agent list --output json` → use `id`
47: - a squad  → `multica squad list --output json` → use `id`
48: 
49: For a person the mention id is the `user_id`, NOT the membership-row id — the
50: backend's own roster formatter uses `user_id` for member mentions. Match by
51: display name. If the name is ambiguous or absent, do not guess — say so in your
52: comment instead of emitting a broken link.
53: 
54: ## Step 2 — the four types and what each enqueues
55: 
56: Format: `[@Name](mention://<type>/<uuid>)`. The `<type>` and the id source must
57: match, or the link resolves to the wrong entity (or to nothing).
58: 
59: | To…                  | type     | uuid from       | What the backend does                                    |
60: | -------------------- | -------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
61: | trigger an agent     | `agent`  | agent.id        | enqueues a run for that agent                            |
62: | hand work to a squad | `squad`  | squad.id        | resolves the squad's `leader_id` and enqueues a run for the LEADER agent |
63: | link a person        | `member` | member.user_id  | renders a link; enqueues NOTHING — no agent run          |
64: | reference an issue   | `issue`  | issue.id        | renders a link; enqueues NOTHING — always safe           |
65: 
66: The backend computes the trigger set from two types only: the `squad` branch
67: resolves the squad and adds its leader to the set; everything that is not
68: `agent` after that is skipped, then the `agent` branch adds that agent. A
69: `member` or `issue` mention reaches neither branch, so it enqueues no task.
70: 
71: A `member` mention therefore does NOT make a person "run", and no notification
72: is delivered through the comment path. What IS guaranteed is the contract above:
73: only `agent` and `squad` mentions enqueue work.
74: 
75: ## Preview and per-comment suppression
76: 
77: Newer clients can call `POST /api/issues/{id}/comments/trigger-preview` before
78: creating or editing a comment. The preview endpoint runs the same trigger
79: computation as create and edit re-triggering, so the displayed agent chips come
80: from backend rules, not from a client-side reimplementation.
81: 
82: When previewing an edit, clients may send `editing_comment_id`. The server
83: validates that the comment belongs to the same workspace and issue, derives or
84: checks the edit's parent comment context, and excludes only pending tasks whose
85: `trigger_comment_id` is that same comment. Pending tasks from any other comment
86: on the issue still dedupe the preview.
87: 
88: When creating or editing a comment, clients may send an optional
89: `suppress_agent_ids` array. The server still computes the full trigger set
90: first, then removes those agent IDs as a post-filter. A missing or empty field
91: preserves the old behavior. A valid UUID that is not in the computed trigger set
92: is a no-op; a malformed UUID is rejected at the request boundary.
93: 
94: ## @all is the broadcast type
95: 
96: `@all` uses the literal `all`, never a UUID:
97: 
98:     [@all](mention://all/all)
99: 
100: It addresses everyone on the issue. It does NOT make any specific agent run.
101: And it is special at trigger time: a comment that carries an `@all` mention is
102: treated as a broadcast that SUPPRESSES the issue assignee's automatic
103: on-comment trigger (and the other implicit routing fallbacks — thread parent /
104: conversation owner). Use `@all` to announce, not to request work from the
105: assignee.
106: 
107: `@all` only suppresses those IMPLICIT routes. An EXPLICIT `@agent` / `@squad`
108: mention in the same comment still fires normally: a comment reading
109: `[@all](mention://all/all) heads up — [@Preflight](mention://agent/<uuid>)
110: please take this` enqueues Preflight and nobody else. The explicit-mention
111: branch is evaluated BEFORE the `@all` short-circuit, so explicit mentions win
112: over the broadcast.
113: 
114: ## What does NOT happen
115: 
116: None of these start a fresh run, and none produce an error response — but they
117: are three different things, and the response tells you which. A mention that
118: never parsed is a truly silent no-op. One that parsed and was refused comes back
119: in `trigger_outcomes` as `status: "blocked"` with a `reason_code`. One whose
120: target has a queued task in the same comment thread can come back `coalesced`.
121: A claim race can return `deferred`: the input is recorded for a follow-up run,
122: not injected into an already running prompt. Different threads queue independently. Read that array after posting — it is the only place any of this shows up.

124: - **A name where a UUID belongs.** `mention://member/Alice` is dead. The id

  "description": "## 任务：CXTE-3 需求澄清与功能拆解（V2 传输加密迁移）\n\n对父单 CXTE-3「加密功能迁移」做需求澄清与功能拆解，产出可评审、可设计的需求文档。\n\n## 公共背景\n\n- 目标工程：`E:\\project\\demo_new`（远端 `http://gitlab.jxbw.com/chenxing/demo_new.git`，分支 `main`，工作区干净，HEAD `9e92da2`；**当前无任何 V2 传输加密代码，属从零迁移**）\n- 迁移依据（唯一权威源，用户指定）：`E:\\project\\demo_new\\迁移说明文档\\transport-v2-migration-guide.md`（v3.0，665 行）\n- 参考代码包：`迁移说明文档\\transport-v2-migration-code\\`（后端 12 个 Java 类 + 前端 2 个 js + 测试资产 T1~T5，可整树拷贝）；前端 UMD 库在 `迁移说明文档\\transport\\sm-crypto-v2-1.15.1.umd.js`\n- 目标形态：§0.2/§2.1 **P3 终局**（明文 `bcprov-jdk15on:1.69` + `bw-funcation-common:4.0.3`，不建 shaded 模块）+ **无 envelope 简化路径**（demo_new 无 envelope 代码，§2.4 三处共存守卫整节跳过）——请在文档中确认该判断\n- 分支：按 skill `branch-policy`；⚠️ 本仓库**无 master**，集成分支是 `main`，拉出基点与合并目标一律为 `main`\n- 用户验收口径：「按迁移说明文档里的说明完成迁移并自测」→ 对应指南 §5.1 / §5.2，未覆盖项按 §5.3 口径如实列出\n\n## 本次拆解要求\n\n1. 按 §1 清单（B1~B14、F1~F6、T1~T5）逐项落到 demo_new 的真实路径，形成**范围覆盖矩阵**（哪些做、哪些整节跳过及跳过依据）。\n2. 对 §0.1 / §0.2 / §0.3 前置条件逐条核对 demo_new 现状（框架版本、过滤器链 order 现状、国密依赖、前端 axios/element-ui 版本），给出「满足 / 不满足 / 需适配」结论；发现指南与 demo_new 现状冲突的地方单列**冲突清单**，这是唯一需要向用户澄清的点。\n3. 把 §5.1（编译与协议自测）、§5.2（18 项浏览器联调用例）转成可验收条目，标注各自的前置条件（是否需启动后端、是否需 token、是否需 DB/Redis），并标出本机环境跑不动、需如实标注「未覆盖」的项。\n4. 不要重新设计协议，不要改动迁移指南本身；指南口径优先于个人判断。\n\n## 产物与落盘\n\n- 需求文档落 `docs/requirements/**`，提交并推送到分支 `doc/CXTE-3-req-split`（从 `main` 拉出）。\n- 完成后在本子单评论交接并 @项目经理（mention 链接形式），附分支名与文档路径。",
